title: Algorithms with Projections
prompt: Implement `topEarner` (max_element with a salary projection) and `sortRoster` (sort by level, ties broken by name — a projection cannot express two keys, so use a comparator) — both without copying the vector.

tests.name: topEarner projects on salary
tests.hint: auto it = std::ranges::max_element(staff, {}, &Employee::salary); return it->name; — {} is the default comparator, the projection is the last argument.

tests.name: sortRoster orders by level then name
tests.hint: std::ranges::sort(staff, [](const Employee& x, const Employee& y) { return x.level != y.level ? x.level < y.level : x.name < y.name; }); — two keys need a comparator, not a projection.
